doc.title: Burrill Crohn interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, January 3, 2012

chapter: Hearing jazz and learning the camera
title: Anne Frank and Maine and first holding a camera
summary: He first wished to shoot himself after watching a cameraman on a 1981 film about Holocaust teaching in Maine.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: At what point did you start going to live things and looking at them as a cameraman, or as a future documentary filmmaker.

Not until I started doing it I don’t think. I mean I really didn’t think that way until I suddenly got the urge. I did a film in 1981, it had nothing to do with jazz, it was called Anne Frank and Maine. A friend of mine was teaching the Holocaust at a little school with Gentile children in Maine, and he brought in the Holocaust as curriculum. And I thought that was just brilliant. And so I pitched the Anti-Defamation League and I got some money to go up there and make a film. And I didn’t shoot or anything at that time, I hired a crew. And I still remember the cameraman I hired and I saw him holding a camera and I saw him shooting, and I said I want to do that. And for the first time he let me hold a camera, oh it felt like so natural. But then he said, I just remember he said, “Shooting is one thing, but that’s the easy part. Lighting. That’s the art. Lighting is where the art comes in.” But I used to dream of having a camera. And then the first documentaries I did I did not shoot, I directed. And they had these beautiful cameras, these old Ikegami cameras. I mean they were seventy thousand dollar cameras. Beautiful

three chip cameras, we shot on one inch tape back then. But I just had a vision of myself having one of these and walking around the street. And one thing led to another and eventually — it was not that one but something like that. But it wasn’t until I started shooting on the portapak that I got a taste of doing that. But it wasn’t for a while until, actually the budgets changed and I had to learn how to do this myself.
